case.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit
case.limits: Section 230 protects the republication of someone else's content. A generated sentence has no other author to point at, and courts have so far been unwilling to assume the answer.
case.holding: Section 230 bars treating an interactive computer service as the publisher of information provided by another, and notice of the content does not remove that protection.
case.why_ai_cites_it: The foundation of every argument that an AI provider is a conduit for material originating elsewhere. Whether a model output counts as information provided by another information content provider is the unresolved question underneath a growing share of AI defamation claims.

reading.body:
Zeran v. America Online is the precedent AI providers cite for immunity, and its limit is that it protects content written by someone else. A generated sentence has no other author to point at.

The 1997 Fourth Circuit holding is narrow on its facts. Section 230 bars treating an interactive computer service as the publisher of information provided by another, and notice of that content does not strip the protection. The doctrine was built for a world where the offending words came from a user and the platform merely carried them. Six live cases now test whether model output fits that description, including Grant v. OpenAI, Askins v. OpenAI Foundation, and four suits against Character Technologies.

That is the unresolved question underneath a growing share of AI defamation claims. If a court reads generated text as information provided by another, the defense holds. If it reads the model as the author, the defense fails at the threshold, before any question of fault or damages is reached. The data does not say which way any court has ruled, only that these cases are live and that the citation is doing work in all of them.

What the record does not cover is the reasoning on either side. It gives the holding, the posture as a defense, and the list of matters citing it, but no outcome in the AI cases and no court's treatment of the authorship question. The reader should treat the six live cases as the place the answer will come from, not as evidence it has arrived.

section.name: AI Case Law: The Precedents Behind the Defenses
